Rashi on Yevamot 14a:10:1.hebrew: מאי קארי לה - הא כבר שנו לעיל: כי אמרינן ״לא תתגודדו״ כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:10:1.english: Why did he ask it - Behold, they already taught above: "When we say [the prohibition of] 'You shall not cut yourselves' [applies]..." etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:12:1.hebrew: מטלטל שרגא - נר שהדליקו בו בשבת וכבה. דסבר לה רבי יהושע כר"ש דלית ליה מוקצה, ור' יוחנן סבר לה כר' יהודה דאית ליה מוקצה, אפי' שלא מחמת איסור:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:12:1.english: Would move a lamp - A lamp that they lit on Shabbat and it went out. For Rabbi Yehoshua holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold of muktzeh; and Rabbi Yoḥanan holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who holds of muktzeh, even [when it is] not due to a prohibition.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:14:1.hebrew: והא איכא שמעא - דרבי אבהו, דלא מסיק אדעתיה ומטלטל באתריה דר' יוחנן, הואיל וחזי לר' אבהו בעלמא דמטלטל:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:14:1.english: But there is a servant - [The servant] of Rabbi Abbahu, who will not realize [this] and will carry in the place of Rabbi Yoḥanan, since he sees Rabbi Abbahu carrying in general.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:16:1.hebrew: בני חייבי לאוין נינהו - הנך דב"ה, שהצרות נישאות לשוק בלא חליצה — אפי' לב"ש דאמרי חליצה בעי — בלאו בעלמא נינהו: "לא תהיה אשת המת". ואין ממזר אלא מחייבי כריתות, כדאמרי' לקמן בהחולץ (יבמות דף מט.):
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:16:1.english: They are children of those liable to negative commandments - Those [children] of Beit Hillel, where the rival wives marry into the general public without ḥalitza — even according to Beit Shammai, who say that ḥalitza is required — are [born of] a mere negative commandment: “The wife of the deceased shall not [be married outside to a stranger]”. And a mamzer is [produced] only from [unions] liable to karet, as we say below in [the chapter entitled] “HaCholetz” (Yevamot 49a).

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:17:1.hebrew: חייבי כריתות נינהו - כיון דצרת הבת פטורה, המייבמה עומד באיסור אשת אח בכרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:17:1.english: They are liable to excision - Since the rival wife of the daughter is exempt [from levirate marriage], one who performs levirate marriage with her remains subject to the prohibition of a brother's wife, [punishable] by excision.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:18:1.hebrew: אין ממזר מחייבי כריתות - אלא מחייבי מיתות ב"ד, כגון: אמו, וחמותו, וכלתו, וכיוצא בהן. וכל הנך דאיסור אחוה, לית בהו מיתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:18:1.english: [There is] no mamzer from [those] liable to karet - But rather from [those] liable to court-imposed death penalties, such as his mother, his mother-in-law, his daughter-in-law, and the like. And all those [cases] of the prohibition of a brother['s wife] do not involve the death penalty.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:19:1.hebrew: דמודעי להו - ב"ש לב"ה: "דעו שהמשפחה זו מצרת ערוה שנתייבמה באה", ופרשו:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:19:1.english: That they would inform them - Beit Shammai [would inform] Beit Hillel: "Know that this family comes from a rival wife of a forbidden relative [ervah] who entered into levirate marriage," and they [Beit Hillel] withdrew.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:20:1.hebrew: ע"ג אלו - משאילין כלים אלו לאלו, וב"ה מחמירין בטהרות טפי:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:20:1.english: [Each] with the other - They would lend vessels to one another, and Beit Hillel are more stringent regarding ritual purity.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:2:1.hebrew: בת קול - בעירובין בפ"ק (דף יג:), יצאה בת קול ואמרה: הלכה כב"ה:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:2:1.english: Divine Voice - In Eruvin, in the first chapter (13b), a Divine Voice went forth and said: "The halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel."

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:4:1.english: Where they are equal to one another - In wisdom.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:5:1.english: This is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehoshua - In the chapter [entitled] “HaZahav” (Bava Metzia 59b).

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:8:1.hebrew: היו כורתים עצים בשבת לעשות פחמים - לבו ביום, כדי לעשות ברזל — איזמל של מילה. דקסבר ר"א: מכשירי מצוה דוחין שבת כמצוה עצמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:8:1.english: They would cut down trees on Shabbat to make charcoal - On that very day, in order to fashion iron — a scalpel for circumcision. For Rabbi Eliezer holds that the preparations for a mitzvah override Shabbat like the mitzvah itself.

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:8:2.hebrew: בשר עוף בחלב - שהיה דורש "בחלב אמו": מי שיש לו חלב אמו, יצא בשר עוף שאין לו חלב אם. והכי אמרי' בפ' כל הבשר:
Rashi on Yevamot 14a:8:2.english: Poultry meat in milk - For he would expound "in its mother's milk": [This applies only to] that which has mother's milk; excluded is poultry meat, which has no mother's milk. And so we say in the chapter [entitled] "Kol HaBasar" [Chullin 113a].

Rashi on Yevamot 14a:9:1.english: A principle was stated by Rabbi Akiva - With regard to circumcision, concerning the prohibition of Shabbat.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:12:1.hebrew: לא הוה מטלטל שרגא - וא"ת: התם משום דהרואה אומר אין צריך לטלטל? וי"ל: דאפילו היה נופל על טליתו, לא היה מטלטל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:12:1.english: "He would not move a lamp" - And if you say: There, [why was his refraining noticeable, since] an onlooker says, "He does not need to move [it]"? And one can answer: Even if it were falling onto his garment, he would not move [it].

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:14:1.hebrew: לא הוה מטלטל משום כבודו של רבי יוחנן - ואע"ג דבסוף שבת (דף קנו: ושם) פסיק רבי יוחנן כר"ש במוקצה מחמת איסור, הכא בהדליקו בו אותה שבת איירי, כדפיר' בקונטרס, דחמיר טפי משום דדחייה בידים. אבל אין לפרש דהכא איירי במוקצה מחמת מיאוס, דהא מוקצה מחמת איסור חמיר טפי, לפירוש ר"ת שפירש בספ"ק דשבת (דף יט: ושם) גבי כרכי דזוזי; ועוד, דעל מוקצה מחמת מיאוס א"ר יוחנן בפ' כירה (שבת ד' מה:): אנו אין לנו בנר אלא כר"ש:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:14:1.english: "He would not carry [it] in deference to Rabbi Yoḥanan" - And even though at the end of Shabbat (156b, and there) Rabbi Yoḥanan ruled in accordance with Rabbi Shimon regarding muktzeh on account of a prohibition, here it is dealing with [a lamp] that they lit on that [same] Shabbat, as explained in the Kunteres [Rashi], which is more stringent because he pushed it away with [his own] hands. But one should not explain that here it is dealing with muktzeh on account of repulsiveness, for muktzeh on account of a prohibition is more stringent according to the interpretation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explained at the end of the first chapter of Shabbat (19b, and there) regarding bundles of coins; and furthermore, regarding muktzeh on account of repulsiveness, Rabbi Yoḥanan said in chapter Kira (Shabbat 45b): "We have [no ruling] regarding a lamp other than in accordance with Rabbi Shimon."

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:16:1.hebrew: בשלמא ב"ש לא נמנעו כו' - וא"ת: ואמאי לא נמנעו משום צרה עצמה, כדאמרי' לקמן בשמעתין? וי"ל: דצרה עצמה לא שכיחא כולי האי כמו בני הצרות, שהאחת יולדת כמה בנים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:16:1.english: "Granted, Beit Shammai did not refrain, etc." - And if you say: Why didn't [Beit Shammai] refrain on account of the rival wife herself, as we say later in our sugya? And one can answer: The rival wife herself is not as common as the children of the rival wives, since one [rival wife] gives birth to several children.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:1:1.hebrew: מי סברת עשו וכו' - תימה, שלא הקשה רבי יוחנן לר"ל מההיא דמייתי בסמוך: "במקומו של ר' אליעזר היו כורתין כו'". וי"ל, דאין חוששין לדקדק כל כך על דבריו — דממילא הוה מוקשה ממגילה, כמו שהקשה בעצמו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:1:1.english: "Do you hold that they acted, etc." - It is puzzling that Rabbi Yoḥanan did not object to Reish Lakish from that [beraita] which [the Gemara] brings nearby: "In the place of Rabbi Eliezer they would cut [wood on Shabbat], etc." And one can say that one is not concerned to be so exacting about his words — since in any case he faced a difficulty from Megillah, just as he himself had objected.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:1:2.hebrew: לא עשו ב"ש כדבריהם - תימה: הא אשכחן דעשו — דהטה ר' טרפון כדברי ב"ש (ברכות דף י:), והלל שהביא עולתו לעזרה וחברו עליו תלמידי שמאי (ביצה דף כ.); ותניא בפרק אלו טרפות (חולין דף מד.): "הרוצה לעשות כדברי ב"ש עושה", ומוקי לה קודם בת קול. ומיהו בלאו הכי מוכח בשמעתין דעשו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:1:2.english: "Beit Shammai did not act in accordance with their statement" - [This is] astonishing, for behold, we find that they acted: for Rabbi Tarfon reclined [to recite the Shema] in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai (Berakhot 10b); and [the incident of] Hillel, who brought his burnt-offering to the Temple courtyard and the disciples of Shammai banded together against him (Beitzah 20a); and it is taught [in a baraita] in the chapter [entitled] "Elu Terefot" (Chullin 44a): "One who wishes to act in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai may act [so]," and [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to the period] before the Heavenly Voice. However, even without this, it is proven in our sugya that they acted.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:5:1.hebrew: רבי יהושע היא דאמר אין משגיחין בבת קול - וא"ת: ומ"ש דלא קי"ל כבת קול דר"א, אלא אמרינן בכל דוכתי דשמותי הוא ואין הלכה כמותו, וכבת קול דב"ה קי"ל דהלכה כב"ה? וי"ל: משום דבת קול דר"א לא יצאה אלא לכבודו, שאמר "מן השמים יוכיחו", כדאמר התם. א"נ, בההיא בת קול שהיתה כנגד רבים, דרבנן הוו רובא — דודאי אין הלכה; אבל כבת קול דב"ה קי"ל, משום דהוו ב"ה רובא, אלא דב"ש מחדדי טפי. וא"ת: ודלמא רבי יהושע נמי דוקא התם קאמר דאין משגיחין, כדפירשנו, אבל בעלמא לא? וי"ל: מדנקט ר' יהושע האי לישנא ואמר "לא בשמים היא", ש"מ דבכל דוכתא אית ליה דאין משגיחין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:5:1.english: "It is Rabbi Yehoshua, who said: One does not pay attention to a Divine Voice" - And if you say: What is the difference, that we do not rule in accordance with the Divine Voice of Rabbi Eliezer, but rather say in every place that he is a shamuti [excommunicated, or a Shammaite] and the halakha is not in accordance with him, yet in accordance with the Divine Voice of Beit Hillel we rule that the halakha is in accordance with Beit Hillel? And one can say: Because the Divine Voice of Rabbi Eliezer came forth only for his honor, since he said, "Let it be proven from Heaven," as [the Gemara] says there [in Bava Metzia 59b]. Alternatively, in that [case], the Divine Voice was against the majority, for the Rabbis were the majority, so certainly the halakha is not [in accordance with it]; however, in accordance with the Divine Voice of Beit Hillel we rule, because Beit Hillel were the majority, [and it was] only that Beit Shammai were sharper. And if you say: But perhaps Rabbi Yehoshua, too, only said there that one does not pay attention [to a Divine Voice], as we explained, but in general, no? And one can say: Since Rabbi Yehoshua used this formulation and said, "It is not in heaven," learn from this that in every place he holds that one does not pay attention [to a Divine Voice].

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:6:1.hebrew: כי אמרי' לא תתגודדו כגון שתי בתי דינין בעיר אחת כו' - וא"ת: מה תירץ ממגילה, דבעיר אחת היו קורין לבני העיר בי"ד, ולבני כפרים היו מקדימים ליום הכניסה? ואומר הרב רבי חיים, דבני כפרים היו קורין בעירם, כדמוכח בירושלמי. והשתא הוו שתי בתי דינים בב' עיירות, דבכי האי גוונא לא שייך "לא תתגודדו" אפילו לאביי. והא דקרי ליה יום הכניסה — לפי שבעירם היו מתאספים לבא לבית הכנסת בשני ובחמישי לקרות התורה. וכן נראה, דאמר בירושלמי דבן עיר אין מוציא בן כרך, דכל שאין מחויב בדבר אין מוציא אחרים ידי חובתם; וכיון שבני הכפרים היו בקיאים לקרות, ודאי היו קורין בעירם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:6:1.english: “When we say ‘You shall not cut yourselves,’ [it is in a case] such as two courts in one city, etc.” - And if you say: What did [the Gemara] answer regarding Megillah? For in one city they would read: for the residents of the city on the fourteenth [of Adar], and for the villagers they would advance [the reading] to the day of entry! And the master, Rabbi Chaim, says that the villagers would read in their [own] town, as is proven in the Yerushalmi. And now [according to this], they are [like] two courts in two [different] towns, as in such a case, “You shall not cut yourselves” does not apply, even according to Abaye. And as for that which [the mishna] calls it “the day of entry” — [this is] because in their [own] town they would assemble to enter the synagogue on Mondays and Thursdays to read the Torah. And so it appears, as [the Gemara] says in the Yerushalmi that a townsperson [ben ir] cannot fulfill the obligation of a walled-city resident [ben karakh], for anyone who is not obligated in a matter cannot fulfill the obligation of others; and since the villagers were proficient in reading [for themselves], they certainly would read in their [own] town.

Tosafot on Yevamot 14a:8:1.english: "In the locale of Rabbi Eliezer," etc. - They would intentionally bring themselves to need [to do] this, out of love for the mitzvah.
